title: Crop Guardian (ফসল রক্ষী) - 3-minute pitch
notes: Every figure is sourced: yield-loss numbers are quoted from the BRRI factsheets in the knowledge base; test counts are from the 20 Nov 2026 local runs (backend 778 + frontend 265). No accuracy or impact figure is claimed.

lines: In Bangladesh, rice feeds the nation.
But when a leaf turns sick, a farmer often has no one to ask.
According to the Bangladesh Rice Research Institute, blast can cut yield by up to eighty percent, and bacterial leaf blight by about thirty.
A wrong guess means the wrong spray, lost money, and a disease that keeps spreading.
Meet Crop Guardian: Fosol Rokkhi, the crop guardian.
A farmer opens a Bangla web app on any phone, picks a division, never an exact location, and photographs one rice leaf.
The photo is cleaned of GPS data, checked for quality, and sent to Meta's Llama 4 vision model, which must answer from a fixed list of nine rice diseases.
If the model is confident, the farmer sees the likely disease with a simple confidence band, never a fake percentage.
Then three to five plain Bangla steps, taken from official rice research factsheets, each with its source.
A validator rejects invented numbers and any pesticide name.
And when the photo is poor or the model is unsure, the app says so: I am not sure.
It gives retake tips and points to the local agriculture office, instead of guessing.
When three photos from one division show the same disease within a week, Crop Guardian drafts an outbreak alert.
Nothing reaches farmers automatically.
A human reviewer approves it, the decision is audit logged, and only then do farmers see: possible outbreak, unverified.
Under the hood: a React app on Vercel, a FastAPI service on Render, and Supabase Postgres with row level security on every table.
The photo itself is never stored.
Retrieval filters the knowledge base by disease and ranks passages by their words. Vector search is planned, not claimed.
More than one thousand automated tests cover the abstain logic, the validator, upload attacks and data isolation.
Claude Code helped us build it, and Claude transcribed the image-only factsheets.
We claim no accuracy figure yet. Our public Trust Centre lists every source and every limit.
Next: a labelled evaluation on Bangladeshi field photos, agronomist review, and more crops.
Cooperatives, NGOs and extension programmes can sponsor it for their farmers.
Crop Guardian. Honest help for every rice field.
